name: HTTP Protocol Foundations for API Design
description: Deep understanding of HTTP protocol semantics as the foundation for designing platform-wide API standards. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: Backend's be_api_design covers a developer's daily implementation of HTTP methods in their own service endpoints (writing controllers, handlers, route definitions); API Design's api_fundamentals_http covers the organization-wide standardization of HTTP protocol usage — defining which status codes are mandatory across all APIs, establishing URI naming conventions in style guides, and setting platform-level content negotiation policies. The backend developer asks 'which HTTP method should my endpoint use?'; the API designer asks 'what HTTP usage standards must all 200+ APIs in our platform follow?'.

subskills.name: HTTP Method Semantics & Platform Standards
subskills.description: Defining organization-wide policies for HTTP method usage — when PATCH vs PUT is mandated, which methods must be idempotent, and how custom methods (WebDAV PROPFIND, REPORT) are governed across all APIs.
keywords: GET POST PUT PATCH DELETE standards

subskills.name: Status Code Taxonomy & Organizational Catalog
subskills.description: Maintaining a curated organizational catalog of permitted HTTP status codes with precise usage guidelines — distinguishing 400 vs 422, mandating 429 response shape, and prohibiting ambiguous codes like 418 or 499 across all teams.

subskills.name: Content Negotiation & Media Type Policies
subskills.description: Designing platform standards for content negotiation using Accept and Content-Type headers, vendor-specific media types (application/vnd.company.v2+json), and serialization format governance (JSON vs Protobuf vs MessagePack).

subskills.name: HTTP Caching Directives & ETag Governance
subskills.description: Establishing platform-wide HTTP caching policies — Cache-Control directive standards, ETag generation strategies (strong vs weak), conditional request (If-None-Match, If-Modified-Since) requirements, and Vary header governance.

subskills.name: CORS Policy Architecture & Preflight Standards
subskills.description: Designing organization-wide CORS policies — allowed origins whitelisting strategies, preflight caching (Access-Control-Max-Age), credential sharing rules, and wildcard vs explicit origin governance for public vs internal APIs.

subskills.name: HTTP/2 & HTTP/3 Protocol Evolution Strategy
subskills.description: Evaluating and planning organizational adoption of HTTP/2 (multiplexing, server push, header compression) and HTTP/3 (QUIC, 0-RTT) — migration strategies, backward compatibility with HTTP/1.1 clients, and API gateway protocol termination.

subskills.name: Idempotency & Safety Contract Standards
subskills.description: Defining platform-wide idempotency contracts — Idempotency-Key header standards, retry-safe operation guarantees, idempotency window TTL policies, and documenting safety/idempotency matrices in API style guides.

subskills.name: URI Design Principles & Naming Conventions
subskills.description: Establishing organizational URI design standards — resource naming conventions (plural nouns, kebab-case vs snake_case), hierarchical path structure depth limits, query parameter naming standards, and URI template (RFC 6570) governance.
